Topics: Reading Literature - Close Reading Of Text
SubTopics: Cite textual evidence and make relevant connections to support analysis of what a literary text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
Content: Which sentence supports the idea that the narrator is a careful observer?

A.Choice: “Most people realize the sea covers two thirds of the planet, but few take the time to understand even a gallon of it.” (paragraph 2)

B.Choice: “People look at you as if you're making it up as you go.” (paragraph 2)

C.Choice: “I rounded the oyster beds, to the far side, relieved to find it relatively crab free.” (paragraph 6)

D.Choice: “It was low tide by then, and I saw the water hesitating at its apex, neither leaving nor returning, patiently waiting for the gravitational gears to shift.” (paragraph 6)

Topics: Reading Literature - Perspective & Purpose In Texts
SubTopics: Determine how an author conveys or develops perspective in a text (through the narrator or speaker when appropriate).
Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
What is the narrator's point of view about most people's relationship with the ocean?

A.Choice: He is critical of people who fail to accurately educate themselves about ocean life.

B.Choice: He believes that people should spend more time enjoying nature than reading about it.

C.Choice: He thinks that people should rely on personal experience rather than charts to explore nature.

D.Choice: He is disappointed that so few people understand the work of fishermen, oystermen, and sailors.

Content: Which detail from paragraph 2 shows how the author develops the narrator's point of view?

A.Choice: “. . . few take the time to understand even a gallon of it.”

B.Choice: “Anyone can tell you where the sun is . . . “

C.Choice: “. . . only fishermen, oystermen and deep-keeled sailors will know without looking.”

D.Choice: “We'd point to charts that showed the Strait of Juan de Fuca inhaling the Pacific . . .”

Topics: Reading Literature - Close Reading Of Text

Content: Which phrase shows that the narrator has a particular goal in searching the bay?

A.Choice: “Most of the time I understated what I saw because I couldn't find words powerful enough” (paragraph 1)

B.Choice: “Almost everything had a market, I was discovering” (paragraph 4)

C.Choice: “I saw a purple ochre star, then fifteen more strewn higher on the beach” (paragraph 5)

Topics: Reading Literature - Perspective & Purpose In Texts
SubTopics: Determine how an author conveys or develops perspective in a text (through the narrator or speaker when appropriate).
Content: Select `bbtext(two)` ways in which paragraphs 3-5 help to develop the narrator's point of view.

A.Choice: The description of the value of different animals shows the narrator's interest in making a profit.

B.Choice: The details about the beauty of the cove at night show the narrator's admiration for the scenery.

C.Choice: The list of materials that the narrator needs shows how hard he is willing to work for his discovery.

D.Choice: The focus on the stress that the narrator feels shows how much he needs to succeed in his search.

E.Choice: The number of animals that the narrator lists shows how much scientific research he thinks is needed.

A.Choice: It describes which marine specimens are best for the narrator's market.

Topics: Reading Literature - Interactions Among Text Elements
SubTopics: Describe how a particular text's structure unfolds in a series of episodes and use textual evidence to describe how the characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution.
Content: How is the narrator affected by his discovery of the nudibranch?

A.Choice: His excitement upon finding a nudibranch causes him to calculate its worth.

B.Choice: His surprise at seeing a nudibranch in the wild interrupts his routine search.

C.Choice: His confusion about the nudibranch's position leads him to search for others.

D.Choice: His amazement at the nudibranch's colors distracts him from catching other creatures.

Topics: Reading Literature - Central Ideas & Themes Of Texts
SubTopics: Determine the theme of a literary text (e.g., stories, plays or poetry) and explain how it is supported by key details; provide a summary of the text distinct from personal opinions or judgments.
Content: This question has `bbtext(two)` parts. First, answer Part A. Then, answer Part B.
What is a theme of the passage?

A.Choice: acting courageously while on an adventure

B.Choice: learning to accept the shortcomings of others

C.Choice: feeling wonder about the treasures of the ocean

D.Choice: understanding that humans and nature need each other

Content: Which detail supports the theme in Part A?

A.Choice: “You'd have to be a scientist, a poet and a comedian to hope to describe it all accurately, and even then you'd often fall short.” (paragraph 1)

B.Choice: “There was no way to make them understand they were tromping across the roofs of clam condos.” (paragraph 2)

C.Choice: “Most people don't want to invest a moment contemplating something like that unless they happen to stroll low tide alone at night with a flashlight . . .” (paragraph 2)

D.Choice: “I loaded up my kayak with a short shovel, a backpack and Ziploc sacks and paddled north out of Skookumchuck Bay . . .” (paragraph 3)
